issues.quote: Herrgott, the regulator on the wall had stopped.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about the atelier regulator clock, its reading, or when it stopped.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the stopped regulator as marking the time of death or the moment of the attack, and try to fit a reading to it that the sheet never provides.

issues.quote: And he had his repeater in his hand.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about a repeater watch, its time, or whether it was running or stopped.
issues.misreading: A repeater is a striking watch, so a solver could read this as a time source in the atelier, or as evidence bearing on when the master's watch was last checked.

issues.quote: The old Morbier, in the hall. You hear it all through the house.
issues.fact: The sheet only says the hall clock struck eleven when the kitchen clock showed 11:03. It does not say the hall clock can be heard throughout the house.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a whereabouts or audibility claim, for example that the strike was audible from the atelier, which bears on who could have heard it.

issues.quote: When she stopped, the kitchen was very quiet.
issues.fact: The sheet only gives the times the piano began and stopped by the kitchen clock. It does not say the piano was audible in the kitchen.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as confirming the kitchen was close enough to hear the piano, which is a whereabouts inference the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: So I went up the stairs to the atelier, and I opened the door, and he was on the floor.
issues.fact: The sheet does not say when Rosa went upstairs, and the transcript does not place the trip relative to the clock readings.
issues.misreading: A solver could assume she went up after the hall clock struck eleven, or during Lina's time in the kitchen, and build a duration or sequence from that unstated order.
